result.summary: This PR is a broad refactor that rewrites numerous fixed-duration calculations across the codebase (GUI time formatting, peer bans, scheduler forwarding, PoW target timing, assumevalid horizon, mempool rolling-fee halflife, relay age limits) to use std::chrono types instead of raw integer seconds. It adds several characterization tests (PoW timing, assumevalid threshold, ROLLING_FEE_HALFLIFE) to pin exact numeric values through the change, and keeps integer interfaces intact where converting them would broaden the diff. The stated goal is purely representational clarity: making implicit time units explicit in the type system rather than in comments, with no intended behavior change.
result.problem: Several duration constants and calculations (ban times, relay-age limits, PoW spacing, assumevalid thresholds) are expressed as raw integers with units documented only in comments, which the author argues risks mixing unrelated integer values and obscures intent for readers less familiar with the surrounding code (janb84: 'It will even provide less proficient in C++ users to read consensus code').

open_concerns: stickies-v is unconvinced the change adds real value beyond cosmetics ('I don't find this harder to read'), a nonblocking sentiment rather than a harm.
PR still needs a rebase (label: Needs rebase) after the latest force-push on 2026-08-18.
resolved_concerns: maflcko's objection that some conversions (e.g. TicksSeconds/count_milliseconds casts) violate util/time.h guidance and add no real type safety was addressed by the author reworking and narrowing the changes (l0rinc: 'I reworked the branch so durations remain typed where the surrounding APIs already support chrono... I like it a lot better this way').
maflcko's confusion about an unrelated ODR-related description was resolved when the author removed that wording from the PR description.
janb84's NIT suggestions to further typify some constants were partially accepted and partially left as-is by design.

result.card: This PR is a repository-wide refactor by l0rinc that re-expresses fixed-duration constants (peer ban times, PoW target timing, assumevalid horizon, relay age limits, mempool rolling-fee halflife) as std::chrono types instead of raw integers, with no intended behavior change and new characterization tests pinning the exact numeric values. The stated problem is readability and avoiding mixing unrelated integer values across time-based constants; janb84 gave a concept ACK for the clarity benefit, while stickies-v and maflcko questioned whether the change adds real safety or clarity, with maflcko's specific technical objections resolved by the author reworking the approach. It touches kernel/chainparams.cpp, txmempool, net_processing.cpp, rpc/node.cpp and blockchain.cpp, validation.cpp, chain.h, and wallet files, but in each area the change is purely representational with values held constant, so it ranks low (P4) everywhere it applies. The PR currently needs a rebase (label: Needs rebase) after six force-pushes, most recently to rebase on a newly merged dependency, #35852. No other PR is reported as depending on this one merging.
